newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds hold their own despite German falls.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds hold their own despite German falls.

text.p: Danish bond prices slipped only slightly on Wednesday despite German falls in a market bolstered by foreign investors with dealers expecting current levels to hold the day out.
"Foreign institutional investors have really been busy buying Danish bonds today, helping to keep prices at high levels despite Germany's correction," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.10 point from the start at 112.16, but up 0.21 point on Tuesday's close, yielding 6.20 percent in turnover of 2.8 billion crowns.
The 2006 benchmark's March future rose 0.04 point to 111.74 with 116 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.37 point to 89.50.
The crown traded at 3.8093 per mark at 1210 gmt, down a pinch from around 3.8090 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 63 during the course of the morning.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling a total of 150 million crowns worth of long-term bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
